12.t: Working with data: speed of sound in materials
q: In which material is sound fastest?
How many times faster is sound in water than in air?
Explain the general pattern for gases, liquids and solids.
Particles are closer together in liquids and solids, so vibrations pass on faster.
A railway worker puts an ear to the track. Explain why the train is heard through the rail before through the air.
Sound travels about 17 times faster in steel than in air, so it arrives much sooner.
